definitions: To transport goods or passengers on the initial or primary leg of a journey, often referring to the most profitable or desired direction of travel for a carrier.
To move a vehicle or vessel in the direction where it is loaded or carrying cargo, as opposed to a back-haul.
examples: The trucking company tries to head-haul as much freight as possible to maximize profits.
They need to head-haul the containers to the main distribution center.
It's more efficient to head-haul goods than to deadhead.
